fuse.name: E_DLOAD_DISABLE
fuse.description: OEM Optional. Disables emergency download via removable SD and/or USB downloader in Apps PBL error handler.

fuse.name: ENUM_TIMEOUT
fuse.description: OEM optional. BOOT ROM must support USB enumeration timeout. Timeout applies to both enumeration for FLCB (fast low current boot) and USB download mode. If USB is not enumerated within time (90 seconds); quit USB enumeration If USB suspend or disconnected after enumeration; start timer again.

fuse.name: FORCE_DLOAD_DISABLE
fuse.description: OEM optional. If FORCE_DLOAD_DISABLE is '0'; device goes to download mode if an error occurs very early in XBL1. If FORCE_DLOAD_DISABLE is set to '1'; device goes into cold boot if an error occurs very early in XBL1.

fuse.name: FORCE_USB_BOOT_DISABLE
fuse.description: OEM optional. If this bit is '0': FORCE_USB_BOOT GPIO when high during boot up; forces boot from USB. If this bit is '1': it disables this feature and FORCE_USB_BOOT GPIO works as a standard GPIO.

fuse.name: SDCC_ADMA_DISABLE
fuse.description: SW only use for Boot ; To disable the ADMA mode of SDCC.

fuse.name: FAST_BOOT
fuse.description: These fuses are used by boot code to specify which device has priority to be booted from. 000:eMMC->SD->USB(SS/FS/HS), 001:SD->eMMC->USB(SS/FS/HS), 010:USB(SS/FS/HS) Boot only, 011:Reserved, 100:SD->USB(SS/FS/HS), 101:eMMC->USB(SS/FS/HS), 110:eMMC->SD->USB(SS/FS/HS), 111:Reserved,.

fuse.name: SPI_CLK_BOOT_FREQ
fuse.description: Default is 37.5 MHz and when blown 19.2 MHz.

fuse.name: SW_FUSE_PROG_DISABLE
fuse.description: It is recommended not to blow this fuse. This fuse disables the ability to blow any more fuses through software. If desired to be blown; this should be blown at the end. Redundant with write permission fuses.

fuse.name: PBL_FDL_TIMEOUT_RESET_FEATURE_ENABLE
fuse.description: Fuse bit to reset device if PBL enters into EDL mode unintentionally. 0x0: NORMAL_MODE 0x1: SECURE_MODE.

fuse.name: WDOG_EN
fuse.description: Prevents WDOG_DISABLE GPIO from disabling WDOG. Frees up the GPIO and prevents potential for abuse by attacker.

fuse.name: PBL_LOG_DISABLE
fuse.description: Used for controlling logging mechanism in PBL. '1' To limit the information collected in PBL logs.

fuse.name: PBL_USB_TYPE_C_DISABLE
fuse.description: Disables type-C functionality during PBL. PBL communication/enumeration happens over USB0_SS only. USB1_SS cannot be used.

fuse.name: ROOT_CERT_TOTAL_NUM
fuse.description: Defines the total root cert number supported from the certificate (Upto 4 roots).

fuse.name: IMAGE_ENCRYPTION_ENABLE
fuse.description: "This bit when blown; is used to indicate that the Image Encryption key regions will be used to store the image encryption root keys. When this bit is unblown; these regions will not be used. Note that this bit only 'enables' the image encryption feature, and is NOT an encryption enforcement bit. With image encryption enabled, the chip can boot with either encrypted or plaintext images (the image has meta-data to indicate if the image is encrypted or not).

fuse.name: DISABLE_ROT_TRANSFER
fuse.description: This fuse permanently disables root of trust transfer.

fuse.name: SW_ROT_USE_SERIAL_NUM
fuse.description: If set; PBL checks that signature covers a serial number that matches that read from fuses. This is for secure boot authentication.

fuse.name: USB_SS_DISABLE
fuse.description: Used to disable USB SS enumeration during Boot.

fuse.name: DEBUG_DISABLE_IN_ROM

fuse.name: ALL_DEBUG_DISABLE

fuse.name: SEC_KEY_DERIVATION_KEY
fuse.description: "This 256-bit value is used as the secondary key derivation input; used to generate the secondary key used by the crypto engine. When running insecure (no secure boot; or Debug enabled) then SKDK is fed into the key derivation function to generate a unique ""non-secure"" secondary key for use by the crypto engine. When running secure (secure boot; and debug disabled); then SKDK is fed directly to the crypto engine as the secondary key.After the SKDK value has been correctly programmed; the SKDK Read Disable should be blown to permanently protect the SKDK value. Prior to this; the SKDK value can be read from the QFPROM by software. The TZ fuse blow API is capable of automatically generating a random number for use as the SKDK so that the SKDK value is never available outside of the device.".
